items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: the Freddies, the Woodys, the Dizzys, the James Moodys, James Spaulding. These are people that I came into contact with.

ctx.x: What is it — you know Phil Woods said that he didn’t consider himself an innovator, he was a craftsman. And maybe — I don’t know how you look at your own playing but does it get harder as time goes by to become an innovator? To come up with something that’s new?

Something that’s completely new? It’s really difficult. We’re in the age of — we’re in the information age on a different level. So there’s so many different things being thrown at us. How does one become an innovator? Well I would say learn as much of the history and gather from it and try to develop your own voice. At this point, like myself as an instrumentalist I just want to be able to tell the story. Hopefully I have my own sound. I’m very derivative of a lot of older people that came before me and I would…

stories which I can’t share here because there’s too much foul language in it. But it’s all good — and it was all very positive stuff. But I take in whatever those people did and the things that I love from recordings by people like Donald Byrd and Art Farmer. And then of course I never really wanted to play trumpet. I wanted to play alto saxophone. And they didn’t have them at the middle school — at the — well junior high school is what we called it back then. They didn’t have them. They didn’t have them. I…
